intended_object: The infimum a ⊓ b of the two elements of an unordered pair {a, b} in a meet-semilattice α. This comes from the docstring and the companion `Sym2.sup`.
explanation: The definition lifts the commutative binary meet `(· ⊓ ·)` to `Sym2 α`, using `inf_comm` as the proof that it is symmetric. So `s(a, b).inf = a ⊓ b`, and this holds by `rfl` (lemma `inf_mk`). A meet-semilattice is the minimal setting in which a binary infimum exists, so the generality is natural. I did not find another Mathlib definition of the infimum of a `Sym2` element; this is the canonical one. (A general fold such as `Finset.inf` works on finsets and would need a bottom element, so it is not the same thing.)
